title: Number of Distinct Islands [dfs multisource]
problemStatement: Depth-first traversal: explore as deep as possible along each branch before backtracking. Foundation for cycle detection, topo prep, components, and path existence.
intuition: DFS is a stack (explicit or call stack). It does not yield shortest unweighted paths, but it is perfect for reachability, component labeling, and path-space search with backtracking.

approaches.title: Recursive DFS
limitations: Deep graphs may hit recursion limit — use iterative

approaches.title: Optimal practical: iterative DFS with explicit stack
approaches.idea: Same idea without recursion depth risk.
approaches.code:
from collections import defaultdict

def dfs_iter(n, edges, src=0):
    g = defaultdict(list)
    for u, v in edges:
        g[u].append(v)
        g[v].append(u)
    seen = [False] * n
    order = []
    st = [src]
    while st:
        u = st.pop()
        if seen[u]:
            continue
        seen[u] = True
        order.append(u)
        for v in reversed(g[u]):  # optional: stabilize order
            if not seen[v]:
                st.append(v)
    return order
approaches.whyWorks: Explicit stack simulates the recursion stack.

edgeCases: Disconnected graph — restart DFS from every unseen node for full cover
commonMistakes: Using DFS distances as shortest paths → WA
patternRecognition: Reachability, components, cycle detection, topo on DAG via finish times
interviewInsight: Mention component restart and recursion-depth tradeoff without being asked.
